threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still taking the bus to get to Dalston when it’s only a 20-minute walk. Everyone knows that’s the best way to soak in those street murals.
Overheard a guy on the bus ranting about how the new strike dates ruin his late-night shift plans. Didn’t know the tube dramas reached the night buses too.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner at 3 AM, mixed with the sound of late-night laughter from the Späti around the corner. That’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here can you stumble upon a spontaneous techno party in a laundromat. The beats mix with the sound of spinning machines—only in Kreuzberg.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they still call it the 'Can', not 'Civic Center' – and don't even flinch when the BART goes down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full gorilla suit catching the 21 Hayes at 6 PM. Muni does bring out the wild side of this city, huh?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about the parks and plazas, but the real treasures are the tiny, forgotten cafés tucked in side streets where locals sip their cortados.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll know them by their fascination with the Passeig de Gràcia; locals just pass by, but they’re busy snapping selfies with the buildings.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground'—you'll learn soon enough how important that distinction is round here.
Saw a guy on the 3 bus serenading everyone with a ukulele. By the time we hit Penge, half the bus was clapping along. Only in South London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy selling homemade falafel from a bike, while a cat nonchalantly crossed the street, ignoring all the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. Grab a döner and check out local artists’ work on the walls!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot a fake taco truck from a mile away—ain't nothing worse than a tourist's Yelp review leading you astray.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the 38 bus line with a ukulele yesterday. He stopped to let a lady with a cane board first. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is just about Gaudí; they miss the hidden gardens where locals sip vermut in peace and share stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how long they take to order a coffee. Locals know it’s 'café amb llet, to go' and not the full menu.
